title: Your PS5 can now emulate PS2 games at up to 120 FPS, strings attached
summary: The new PS5SX2 v2.00 update brings frame generation and 8x scaling, but emulators on PS5 require a rather easy jailbreak.
body: Credit: Dhruv Bhutani / Android Authority TL;DR Popular PS2 emulator for PS5, PS5SX2, just received its v2.00 update, introducing built-in frame generation (up to 120fps), up to 8x resolution scaling on PS5 Pro, one-click HD texture packs, and restored online multiplayer for some games. The update comes on the back of the recent Relapse exploit that makes it fairly easy to jailbreak a PS5 as long as it is running firmware v13.60 or lower. The PS5 jailbreak community has seen a surge in activity this month, most of it riding the back of the new Relapse exploit , which allows any PlayStation 5 with firmware version 13.60 or earlier to be successfully jailbroken. This firmware was released in July 2026, so as long as you skipped the recent v14.xx updates, you can quite easily run homebrew apps and even a Nintendo Switch emulator on your PS5 . If you need even more reason to consider jailbreaking your PS5, one of the most popular PS2 emulators just received a massive upgrade that lets you play classic PS2 games on your current console. Developer sword_pdf has rolled out PS5SX2 v2.00 , a major update to the standalone PlayStation 2 emulator built for jailbroken PS5 consoles.

title: Linux app support is disappointing on Googlebooks, but Breadstick Linux is the solution

body: Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority TL;DR The Breadstick Linux app is available on the Play Store and offers improvements over native Linux support on Android and Googlebooks. Unlike the Terminal app on Googlebooks, Breadstick Linux offers a desktop mode, an easy setup process, and quick access to recommended apps. The app is available as a free version, but you can also buy the Pro version for a one-time fee of $20. Googlebooks have plenty of selling points, such as deep cross-device support, Gemini integration, and Android app support. The platform can also run Linux apps via the Android Terminal , but this functionality is barebones and relies on unwieldy commands. Fortunately, a third-party app has stepped in with much better support. Breadstick Linux has emerged as an alternative to native Linux support on Googlebooks. This app is available via the Play Store and runs a custom version of the Debian Linux distribution via a container. The developer initially created the app for phones and tablets, but has now tuned it to run on the Google-powered laptops. Furthermore, the latest version of the app now supports Intel-based Googlebooks.

title: Google just gave Gemini a new role to fill at work, and it’s a big one
summary: Your next coworker might be AI, and it already has email.
body: TL;DR Google has introduced a new universal Gemini agent that can complete multi-step tasks across apps without constant user input. The agent works with Google Workspace, Slack, and Microsoft 365, maintains context across devices, and can use specialized AI sub-agents. It’s currently available only to enterprise customers in private preview, with no word on a wider consumer release. AI tools have become pretty good at helping us get things done, but we still have a lot of work to do ourselves. Sure, Gemini can summarize a lengthy email thread, help draft a document, or pull information from a spreadsheet. But what if you could tell it what you want to accomplish and let it handle the rest? That’s pretty much what Google is working toward with its latest announcement . At Gemini at Work 2026, Google Cloud introduced a new Gemini agent that can take on entire tasks, work across different apps, and deliver finished results without requiring you to guide it through every step.

title: Amazon’s latest tablets finally come with the Google Play Store baked right in
summary: The top-of-the-line Alexa Tablet 12 Pro will be available with an optional Nanomatte finish for reduced display glare.
body: TL;DR Amazon has released its first-ever range of tablets with the Google Play Store built in, plus a premium aluminum unibody design and powerful internal hardware. The Alexa Tablet 12 Pro is the top-of-the-line variant and will be available with a Nanomatte finish for anti-glare properties. Amazon has also released 8.7-inch and 11-inch kids’ tablets, with variants designed specifically for children over the ages of three and six. Amazon has produced a long list of Fire tablets over the past 15 years. These tablets run Fire OS, a forked version of Android, and lack access to Google Mobile Services (GMS). As a result, they can’t access apps and games from the Google Play Store. Amazon has now rectified this particular shortcoming with its new range of tablets. The retail giant today announced the Alexa Tablet 12 Pro, the Tablet 11, and the Tablet 8, featuring full access to the Play Store and a premium aluminum unibody design.
